prompt: When $(2x - 3)(x + 5)$ is expanded and written in the form $ax^2 + bx + c$, what is the value of $b$?
hint: The question asks only about the $x$ term. Think about which of the four products in the expansion contain exactly one $x$.

hints.text: The question asks only about the $x$ term. Think about which of the four products in the expansion contain exactly one $x$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller binomials: $(x + 1)(x + 2) = x^2 + 3x + 2$, where the middle term $3x$ came from $2x + x$. Only the outer and inner products make an $x$ term.
The outer product is $2x \cdot 5$ and the inner product is $-3 \cdot x$. Work out both of them and add the results.
The two products are $10x$ and $-3x$, which combine to $7x$. The value of $b$ is $7$.

learningObjective: Extract a single coefficient from a binomial product.
explanation: Multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second: $(2x - 3)(x + 5) = 2x^2 + 10x - 3x - 15$.
Combine the two like terms in the middle to get $2x^2 + 7x - 15$.
Matching this with $ax^2 + bx + c$ shows that the coefficient of $x$ is $7$, so $b = 7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Target just the term you need
steps: The $x$ term comes only from the outer and inner products of FOIL.
Skipping the first and last products saves time and removes two chances to make a sign error.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Answering −15 gives c, and 10 gives only the outer product — b needs BOTH cross terms.
The x-coefficient is outer plus inner: 10x + (−3x) = 7x. Collect the pair before reporting.
